answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 6 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The umber multiplier is published, charged in violet, and comet lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4352 identities would post 1422 proofs and burn roughly 48 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
